name: Intervals
tagline: Sort by start. Then only the last one can overlap.
template:
def merge(intervals):
    out = []
    for start, end in sorted(intervals):    # sort by start
        if out and start <= out[-1][1]:      # overlaps the last one kept
            out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], end)
        else:
            out.append([start, end])
    return out

print(merge([[1, 3], [8, 10], [2, 6]]))  # -> [[1, 6], [8, 10]]
complexity: O(N log N) for the sort, then O(N)

blocks.html:
A calendar: two meetings clash when one starts before the other ends.

Checking every pair is O(N²). Sort by start time first, and each interval only needs to look at the one before it.

blocks.code:
def slow(meetings):                # brute force: at each start, count who is in a room, O(N^2)
    best = 0
    for s, _ in meetings:
        busy = sum(1 for a, b in meetings if a <= s < b)
        best = max(best, busy)
    return best

def fast(meetings):                # sweep: sorted starts vs sorted ends, O(N log N)
    starts = sorted(s for s, _ in meetings)
    ends = sorted(e for _, e in meetings)
    rooms = best = j = 0
    for s in starts:
        while ends[j] <= s:        # someone left before this start: free a room
            rooms -= 1
            j += 1
        rooms += 1
        best = max(best, rooms)
    return best

for meetings in [[[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]], [[1, 5], [5, 8]], [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]]]:
    print(slow(meetings), fast(meetings))  # -> 2 2, then 1 1, then 3 3
blocks.note: Count overlaps at every start, then one sweep over sorted times

blocks.html: Once intervals are sorted, you only compare with the last one kept, or with the earliest end. Sorting turns an all-pairs check into one pass.

options: It depends on the sort order
blocks.why: The first ends exactly when the second starts, so the room is free again. That is why the sweep frees on ends[j] <= s.

pitfalls: Sort by start first; merging unsorted intervals misses overlaps.
Decide whether touching ends overlap (<= or <). The problem statement tells you.
When merging, take the max of the ends: a later interval can sit fully inside the last one.
